newsitem.title: USA: Canada LPG market tumbles on U.S. weakness.
newsitem.headline: Canada LPG market tumbles on U.S. weakness.

text.p: Canada liquefied petroleum gases (LPG) continued to fall this week, caught in the downdraft of plummeting U.S. prices and a market heavy with sellers, players said Thursday.
"Everyone is keeping their eyes on Belvieu (Texas) and with the weather warmer than normal people think they can skinny through the rest of winter," said one eastern Canada trader.

In the east, Sarnia hub spot propane prices fell 8.75 cents to between 45.00 cents and 46.25 cents a gallon. Traders said the market is likely to continue to fall to within a 4.00 cent spread with Belvieu.

In western Canada, Edmonton propane prices fell 5.25 cents to 38.50/39.00 cents in light to moderate trade. Exports were continuing to chug along through the Cochin pipeline to feed the U.S. Midwest markets, traders said.
Normal butane traded between 47.50/48.75 cents, also weaker due to falling U.S. values.
